items.title: Cherkes Ethem
items.notes: Cherkes Ethem (1886–1948) was a prominent Circassian guerrilla leader who became a vital militia commander in the early stages of the Turkish War of Independence. Leading the irregular Kuvâ-yi Seyyâre (Mobile Forces), he initially earned national acclaim for stalling the Greek military advance and suppressing internal anti-revolutionary rebellions. However, his independent stance and refusal to merge his forces into the newly established regular Turkish army led to a bitter conflict with the central Ankara government. Declared a traitor and rebel in late 1920, he was defeated and spent the remainder of his life in exile.

items.title: Kabardian horse
items.notes: The racehorse Gastroler ( foaled in 1935, by Istorik out of Geparda) is registered as an elite representative of the Kabardian breed (Кабардинская порода). He was bred at the Malka Stud Farm (Malocherkesky No. 34), located in Kabardino-Balkaria. Gastroler belonged to the foundational Istorik line, which remains one of the active and most important sire lines in the history of the Kabardian breed.

The photo was taken in Moscow at the All-Union Agricultural Exhibition (VSHV)—known today as the VDNH Exhibition Complex. It was captured during the historic 1939 exhibition. Gastroler belonged to the foundational Istorik line, which remains one of the active and most important sire lines in the history of the Kabardian breed.

items.title: A wedding in Tugurgoy
items.notes: A wedding in the village of Tugurgoy, Adygea, from 1909.Boris Nikolaevich Ustinov the modern archival historian and collector who rescued and compiled this series for the public. items.title: Healing music ritual
items.names: Shach Chukbar, laying: Khoza Ampar, and Alexa Ampar
items.originalNames: Чукбар Шач, Ампар Хоза (Гуаза), Ампар Алыкса
items.notes: The image shows Abkhazian folk singer and storyteller Shach Chukbar playing an apkhartsa (a two-stringed bowed instrument) at the bedside of the ailing Khoza Ampar in Abkhazia, around 1929. Performances like this were used to comfort the sick, promote healing, and soothe spirits.
